blueprint_concepts: Image of a line in a line; reflection of a light ray

concept_use.Image of a line in a line; reflection of: The reflected ray is the image of the incident line AP in the mirror; it passes through the image A' of A and meets the x-axis at Q(3,0).
concept_use.Reflection property of Ellipse: The reflection property of the ellipse shows that the ellipse with foci A, Q touches the mirror at P, so 2a = AP + PQ = 10 and e = 3/5.

english: A ray of light passing through the point $A(-3,0)$ strikes a plane mirror lying along the line $16x+15y=100$ at the point $P\left(4,\frac{12}{5}\right)$ and is reflected. The reflected ray meets the $x$-axis at $Q$. Let $E$ be the ellipse with foci $A$ and $Q$ that touches the line $16x+15y=100$. Then the eccentricity of $E$ is
hindi: बिन्दु $A(-3,0)$ से होकर जाती एक प्रकाश किरण रेखा $16x+15y=100$ के अनुदिश रखे समतल दर्पण पर बिन्दु $P\left(4,\frac{12}{5}\right)$ पर टकराकर परावर्तित होती है। परावर्तित किरण $x$-अक्ष से $Q$ पर मिलती है। माना $E$ वह दीर्घवृत्त है जिसकी नाभियाँ $A$ तथा $Q$ हैं और जो रेखा $16x+15y=100$ को स्पर्श करता है। तब $E$ की उत्केन्द्रता है
solution: The reflected ray is the image of line $AP$ in the mirror; it passes through $A'$, the image of $A$
Reflection property: an ellipse with foci $A,Q$ touching the mirror touches it at $P$ (equal angles at $P$), so $2a=AP+PQ$
solution_full: By the law of reflection, the reflected ray lies along the image of the incident line $AP$ in the mirror, so it passes through $A'$, the image of $A$ in $16x+15y-100=0$.

Reflection property of the ellipse: the normal at any point of an ellipse bisects the angle between the focal radii. For the ellipse with foci $A,Q$ that touches the mirror line, the point of contact is the point where a ray from $A$ reflects through $Q$, which is $P$. Hence $P$ lies on $E$.
Check: $E$ is $\dfrac{x^2}{25}+\dfrac{y^2}{16}=1$; $P$ lies on it ($\frac{16}{25}+\frac{9}{25}=1$) and its tangent at $P$ is $\frac{4x}{25}+\frac{3y}{20}=1$, i.e. $16x+15y=100$.
originality_note: New: a plane-mirror reflection is used to locate the second focus, and the reflection property of the ellipse is used backwards to identify the point of contact of the ellipse with the mirror line (way 5: the link between the two reflection laws is the discovery). Closest known: 'a ray from one focus reflects through the other focus'. Different because: the ellipse is not given; its second focus and its point of contact must be found from the plane mirror.
stem_review: Read as a student: every point, line, curve and symbol is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy/mpmath (and a numerical brute-force check), is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Checked that A and Q lie on the same side of the mirror and that the ellipse with foci A, Q touching the line is unique. Changed: No change.
key_step: Reflected ray through the image of A gives Q; the reflection property gives the contact point P, so 2a = AP + PQ.
justification: A routine chain (image of a point, intersection, focal-sum definition) with one recognition that the contact point is P. Comparable to 2024-P1-Q4 (L2), an ellipse fixed from tangent data.
